title: Senior's toolkit: on call with kubectl and Helm
summary: Events, previous logs, ephemeral debug containers, can-i, diff, server-side apply and Helm releases.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: on call with kubectl and Helm
steps.body: The incident commands: what happened, what the crashed container said, a shell into a distroless pod, and a safe release with a way back.

toolkit.what: Recent events in time order: scheduling failures, image pulls, probe failures, kills. The first stop when you do not know what broke.
flags: the newer command, events for one object

toolkit.what: The logs of the previous, crashed container. Without `-p` you see the fresh restart, which has not failed yet.
flags: pick a container in a multi-container pod
all pods with a label, each line tagged

toolkit.what: Adds an ephemeral debug container that shares the target's process namespace. Works on distroless images that have no shell.
flags: the container whose processes you want to see
`kubectl debug node/x -it --image=...`: a pod on the node with the host filesystem at `/host`

toolkit.what: Asks the API server whether a user or service account may do something. Settles RBAC questions without trial and error.
flags: ask on behalf of a service account
toolkit.example: kubectl auth can-i create deployments -n shop --as=system:serviceaccount:shop:deployer

toolkit.what: Shows what `apply` would change, computed by the server. Exit code 1 means there are differences.
The API server merges the change and records which tool owns each field. Conflicts with other owners are reported instead of silently overwritten.
flags: take ownership of fields another manager set, on purpose

toolkit.what: Installs or upgrades a release in one idempotent command, waits for it, and rolls back automatically if it does not become healthy. Helm 3 calls the flag `--atomic`.
flags: install if the release does not exist yet
wait, and roll back on failure (Helm 3: `--atomic`)

toolkit.what: Lists a release's revisions and returns to one. `helm template ... | kubectl diff -f -` previews a change before you run it.
toolkit.example: helm history api -n shop && helm rollback api 7 -n shop

steps.prompt: A pod restarts every 30 seconds. `kubectl logs api-x` shows only the start-up banner and nothing else. What do you run first?
options: `kubectl logs api-x -p` and `kubectl describe pod api-x`
steps.explain: Plain `logs` shows the new container, which has not crashed yet. `-p` shows the one that died, and `describe` shows the last state (exit code, OOMKilled) and probe failures, often a liveness probe killing a slow start.

steps.prompt: Match the flag to its meaning.
pairs: logs of the previous, crashed container
share the process namespace of container `api`
check permissions on behalf of someone else
let the API server merge and track field owners
install if missing, upgrade if present

steps.prompt: Get a shell next to a distroless container that has no `sh` of its own.
steps.explain: `kubectl exec` needs a shell inside the image. `debug` adds an ephemeral container with your own tools, and `--target` lets it see the app's processes.

steps.prompt: The CI pipeline fails with `deployments.apps is forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:shop:deployer" cannot patch resource "deployments"`. How do you confirm the fix before re-running the pipeline?
options: `kubectl auth can-i patch deployments -n shop --as=system:serviceaccount:shop:deployer` should print `yes`
Re-run the pipeline until it passes
steps.explain: `can-i --as` asks the authorizer directly, in seconds. Add the verb to the Role, apply it, check with `can-i`, then re-run.

steps.prompt: Put a careful manual release with Helm in order.
lines: helm template api ./chart -f values-prod.yaml | kubectl diff -f -
also: helm template api ./chart -f values-prod.yaml | kubectl diff -f -
steps.explain: Preview, release with automatic rollback, then check what happened. The two checks at the end can go in either order.

steps.prompt: Safe to run during an incident without changing anything, or does it change the cluster?
steps.explain: `debug` adds an ephemeral container to the pod spec: harmless, but it is a change and it stays until the pod is replaced.

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: On call, start with events and `logs -p`, then `describe`, and reach for `kubectl debug` instead of baking shells into images. Never apply by hand without a `diff`, and release with Helm's automatic rollback so a failed deploy undoes itself.
